issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims (abstract, introduction, Section 3) that the derived conditions ensure nearly optimal O(N^{-1+eps}) RQMC rates via Owen's boundary growth theory. What is actually derived in Sections 3.2.1-3.2.3 is only the limit of the ratio phi/psi (finite or zero), i.e. boundedness of the transformed integrand near the boundary. Owen's result, as the paper itself states, requires growth bounds on all mixed partial derivatives of the transformed integrand (which involve 1/psi(Psi^{-1}(u_j)) factors that blow up at the boundary), plus corner-avoidance properties of the point set. None of these is checked; boundedness alone does not imply finite Hardy-Krause variation or the rate. The rate claim is therefore unsupported by the analysis.

failure_location.quote: Then, we tune the parameters of the proposal density to satisfy the derived boundary growth conditions that ensure nearly optimal convergence rates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the claims to 'necessary conditions for boundedness of the transformed integrand, empirically observed to restore the rate', or add an argument verifying Owen-type growth conditions for the mixed partial derivatives of the transformed integrand under the chosen parameters (case (ii)/(iii)).
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification for the advertised 'nearly optimal' rate of RQMC under the proposed transformations is missing; only empirical evidence supports it. Statements in the abstract, introduction, Section 3.1 and 3.2 that the conditions 'ensure' the rate are overclaims.
issues.title: Boundedness-only 'boundary growth conditions' claimed to ensure nearly optimal RQMC rates
issues.why_classification: A contained (but nontrivial) derivative-growth argument, or a limited weakening of the advertised guarantee to boundedness plus empirical rates, resolves it without changing the method or experiments.

issues.failure_explanation: With nu_tilde = 2T/nu - d, the exponent in h_1^{VG} equals -(T/nu)[log(y'Sigma y) - log(y'Sigma_tilde^{-1} y)], so h_1^{VG} = const * (y'Sigma_tilde^{-1}y / y'Sigma y)^{T/nu}, a ratio of two positive-definite quadratic forms, homogeneous of degree 0 and bounded between the extreme generalized eigenvalues. Hence the limit as u_j -> 0 is a finite positive number for every Sigma_tilde: case (i) (limit +infinity when Sigma - Sigma_tilde^{-1} < 0) and case (iii) (limit 0 when > 0) are both false; only case (ii) is correct. The stated dependence of singularity removal on the 'interplay' of nu_tilde and Sigma_tilde at this nu_tilde is spurious.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (eq:mvg_conditions_1) by the correct statement that for nu_tilde = 2T/nu - d the ratio is bounded for any Sigma_tilde > 0 (limit depends on direction), and keep only the nu_tilde-based case split (eq:mvg_conditions_2) as the effective boundary growth condition.
issues.overall_effect: The first alternative rule for multivariate VG in Table tab:multivariate_dom_tranf (nu_tilde = 2T/nu - d and Sigma - Sigma_tilde^{-1} >= 0) is based on an incorrect case analysis; the rule still yields a bounded ratio, so no experiment is invalidated, but the derivation and the claimed role of Sigma_tilde are wrong.
issues.title: Multivariate VG limit cases wrong: with nu_tilde = 2T/nu - d the ratio is a bounded degree-0 quotient
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the case analysis; the recommended parameter choices remain valid and no result or experiment is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The asymptotic Laplace density (eq:lap_pdf_as_exp) contains, besides the exponential, the algebraic prefactor (Q/2)^{v/2} / sqrt(2 sqrt(2Q)) with Q = y'Sigma_tilde^{-1}y and v = (2-d)/2, i.e. |y|^{(1-d)/2}. Its reciprocal |y|^{(d-1)/2} multiplies r^{NIG} but is omitted from h_1^{NIG} in (eq:T_NIG). When the exponents cancel exactly (case (ii), the construction Sigma_tilde = 2/(delta^2 T^2) Delta^{-1} adopted in the text and Table tab:multivariate_dom_tranf), r^{NIG} grows like |y|^{(d-1)/2} -> infinity for d >= 2, not to sqrt(det Sigma_tilde). Thus the stated sufficient condition with '>= 0' is not sufficient at equality; only the strict case (iii) yields decay.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the algebraic prefactor in h_1^{NIG}, replace the condition by strict definiteness delta^2 T^2 Delta - 2 Sigma_tilde^{-1} > 0, and choose Sigma_tilde = (2+eps)/(delta^2 T^2) Delta^{-1} with eps > 0 (or note the polynomial growth is offset by the payoff transform decay).
issues.overall_effect: The recommended multivariate NIG rule does not achieve the announced boundedness of the ratio phi/psi for d >= 2; the transformed integrand is bounded only if the payoff transform decays fast enough to compensate the polynomial growth. The univariate case d = 1 is unaffected.
issues.title: Multivariate NIG: polynomial prefactor of the Laplace density dropped, so the equality choice Sigma_tilde = 2/(delta^2 T^2) Delta^{-1} leaves an unbounded ratio for d >= 2
issues.why_classification: A short local correction (strict inequality / small inflation of Sigma_tilde) restores the intended guarantee without changing the method, experiments, or any other claim.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark justifies reusing the damping rule of [bayer2022optimal] by arguing that the transformed integrand at the origin is g(0)/psi(0) with psi(0) a finite constant. For the multivariate Laplace density (eq:mlap_pdf) with v = (2-d)/2, K_v(x) ~ -log x (d = 2) or ~ x^{-|v|} (d >= 3), so psi_lap(y) -> infinity as y -> 0 and psi_lap(0) is not a finite constant; the transformed integrand vanishes at the origin and its peak is not there. Moreover, under the mixture representation (prop:nig_proposition, prop:vg_proposition) the inner integrand additionally depends on w. The claimed independence of the optimal damping parameter from the transformation is therefore unsupported for the multivariate NIG (and mixture) settings.
